While the past year had been increasingly stressful with contracts drying up and my savings getting tight, losing that final promising contract a month ago was definitely the final straw that triggered this deep, joyless state.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up in the morning anymore' - are you having thoughts of actively wanting to end your life, or is it more of a passive wish to not exist?\n\nPatient: It started out as just a passive wish to not wake up, just wanting the constant worry to stop. But on a few really dark days, it has crossed over into picturing how I might actually end things. I haven't made a concrete plan or acted on it, but the thoughts have definitely been there.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned that the loss of the consulting contract a month ago seemed to trigger this episode, but can you clarify if you're experiencing a persistent low mood or if there are brief periods where your mood slightly improves, even if it returns to feeling low?\n\nPatient: No, it has been completely constant. Since that contract fell through, it’s just been a continuous, heavy cloud hanging over me without any breaks or moments where my mood lifts. I feel this way every single day, with no relief at all.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that your low mood has been constant since the contract fell through, but can you think of any specific situations or events, no matter how small, that have briefly improved your mood or reduced your feelings of sadness, even if it was just for a short time?\n\nPatient: No, I can't really think of anything that has briefly improved my mood or brought me joy lately. It honestly feels like that capacity has been completely switched off in my brain. Even small things that used to make me happy just don't register at all anymore.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any changes in your movement or speech, such as feeling slowed down or restless, since you've been feeling this way?\n\nPatient: I haven't really noticed any specific changes in my speech or feeling physically restless. However, I do feel completely exhausted all the time, and my thinking has felt incredibly slow lately.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned feeling exhausted and your thinking has felt slow, but can you tell me more about whether you've experienced any physical slowing down of your movements, such as taking longer to get dressed or move around, since you've been feeling this way?\n\nPatient: I haven't really noticed myself physically moving slower or taking longer to do tasks like getting dressed. It’s more that absolutely everything feels like it requires a massive amount of effort because I am so constantly exhausted.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned that nothing brings you joy anymore, but have you experienced any activities or situations that you used to dislike but now find neutral or less bothersome since you've been feeling this way?\n\nPatient: I haven't really noticed anything like that happening. Rather than disliked things becoming more neutral, everything in general just feels completely flat, gray, and devoid of any energy or interest.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you've been taking care of your daily needs, such as bathing, dressing, and grooming, since you've been feeling this way, and have you noticed any difficulty or slowness in performing these tasks?\n\nPatient: Honestly, even simple daily tasks like taking a shower or getting ready feel like a massive chore now. I feel constantly wiped out, and doing these basic things takes so much more effort and time than it used to. It just leaves me feeling completely drained.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned this is your first episode of feeling this way and it started after a significant life event, but can you tell me if you've had any periods of elevated mood or irritability in the past, even if not as severe as your current state?\n\nPatient: No, I’ve never experienced anything like that. My mood has always been relatively stable and steady, without any periods of abnormally high energy or unusual irritability, until this recent downward turn.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any episodes of feeling excessively restless or agitated, where you couldn't sit still, since you've been feeling this way?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't felt restless or agitated at all. If anything, it’s the exact opposite—I feel incredibly sluggish and heavy. I can easily sit staring at my workbench for hours without moving a muscle.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned feeling sluggish and heavy, but can you tell me if there have been any times when you felt like you were moving or talking more slowly than usual, to the point where others might have noticed?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure about that, and I haven't noticed myself moving or talking slower. Since I've been keeping to myself and canceling plans lately, there hasn't really been anyone around to comment on it anyway.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed or has anyone else pointed out that you seem to be moving or responding more slowly than usual, even if it's just in small ways like slower reactions or taking longer to answer questions?\n\nPatient: I haven't really noticed myself moving or speaking slower, and no one has mentioned anything like that to me. My mind itself definitely feels quite slow and foggy lately, though, like it's taking forever just to process basic thoughts.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any instances where your physical movements or speech seemed slower to you or were pointed out by someone else as being slower, which might help differentiate between the severity of your current state?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really noticed my physical movements or speech being slower, and no one has mentioned anything like that to me. It's really just my mind that feels incredibly bogged down and sluggish.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if there have been moments, even small ones, where you felt like your body was moving in slow motion or that it took noticeable effort to initiate physical movements, which might help us understand your condition better?\n\nPatient: I wouldn't say I've thought of it as \"slow motion\" specifically, but initiating even basic physical tasks like taking a shower or walking to the grocery store requires an immense amount of physical effort. Everything just feels incredibly heavy, exhausting, and hard to start, and it leaves me completely wiped out.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any specific examples or days where it took you an unusually long time to perform daily tasks, such as getting out of bed, eating, or engaging in any physical activity, compared to your normal pace before this episode started?\n\nPatient: Yes, absolutely. I can sit in my workshop for an hour just staring at a project without ever starting it, and my brain feels so much like molasses that writing a simple email takes ages of rereading and second-guessing. I also regularly forget to eat until late afternoon, and basic tasks like walking to the grocery store now feel far more exhausting than a long bike ride ever did.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any specific days or moments where others, like friends or family, noticed that you were moving or responding more slowly than usual, which might have been different from your normal behavior?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't noticed anyone commenting on me moving or speaking slowly, and since I've been keeping to myself so much lately, I haven't really been around people enough for them to notice anyway.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling exhausted and like everything requires a lot of effort, but can you specifically describe if you've experienced any days where it was unusually hard to get out of bed or start your daily activities, and if so, how that compared to your usual self before this episode?\n\nPatient: Yes, getting out of bed and starting the day has become a real uphill battle. Because I lie awake worrying until 2 or 3 in the morning, I wake up completely unrefreshed, and basic things like showering now feel like climbing a mountain. Before this, I was highly active, regularly going on long bike rides along Lake Michigan or spending hours working on my woodworking and model trains without a second thought.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe in more detail how your physical movements or ability to initiate actions have changed since you started feeling this way, such as any difficulty starting tasks or a feeling of being physically slowed down?\n\nPatient: I feel incredibly slowed down and really struggle to initiate any action. I often go down to my workshop and just sit there for long stretches staring at my projects, completely unable to actually start anything. Even simple physical tasks like taking a shower or walking to the grocery store now require a massive amount of physical effort, leaving me constantly wiped out.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned that this episode started after losing the consulting contract, but can you tell me if you think this event alone triggered your current state, or if you believe there were other underlying factors that contributed to how you're feeling now?"

I have almost no appetite and lie awake until 2 or 3 in the morning with my mind looping over worries, and I feel so completely wiped out that even taking a shower is exhausting.\n\nDoctor: Have you been experiencing feelings of worthlessness or guilt, or have you been having thoughts that you're a burden to others or that you've let them down?\n\nPatient: Yes, I keep telling myself that losing those consulting contracts was entirely my fault and that I’ve let everyone down. I feel like complete deadweight lately, and I've caught myself thinking my sister and my ex would honestly be better off without me around.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any thoughts of death or suicidal ideation, or have you considered harming yourself in any way since you've been feeling this way?\n\nPatient: To be honest, yes. I regularly find myself thinking it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up in the morning anymore. On a couple of really bad days, I've even pictured how I might end things, though I haven't actually acted on those thoughts.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced episodes like this before, or is this the first time you've felt this way, and do you think the loss of the consulting contract triggered this episode or was it just the final straw?\n\nPatient: This is the first time I’ve ever felt this way, and it is completely unlike me. While the past year had been increasingly stressful with contracts drying up and my savings getting tight, losing that final promising contract a month ago was definitely the final straw that triggered this deep, joyless state.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up in the morning anymore' - are you having thoughts of actively wanting to end your life, or is it more of a passive wish to not exist?\n\nPatient: It started out as just a passive wish to not wake up, just wanting the constant worry to stop. But on a few really dark days, it has crossed over into picturing how I might actually end things. I haven't made a concrete plan or acted on it, but the thoughts have definitely been there.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned that the loss of the consulting contract a month ago seemed to trigger this episode, but can you clarify if you're experiencing a persistent low mood or if there are brief periods where your mood slightly improves, even if it returns to feeling low?\n\nPatient: No, it has been completely constant. Since that contract fell through, it’s just been a continuous, heavy cloud hanging over me without any breaks or moments where my mood lifts. I feel this way every single day, with no relief at all.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that your low mood has been constant since the contract fell through, but can you think of any specific situations or events, no matter how small, that have briefly improved your mood or reduced your feelings of sadness, even if it was just for a short time?\n\nPatient: No, I can't really think of anything that has briefly improved my mood or brought me joy lately. It honestly feels like that capacity has been completely switched off in my brain. Even small things that used to make me happy just don't register at all anymore.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any changes in your movement or speech, such as feeling slowed down or restless, since you've been feeling this way?\n\nPatient: I haven't really noticed any specific changes in my speech or feeling physically restless. However, I do feel completely exhausted all the time, and my thinking has felt incredibly slow lately.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned feeling exhausted and your thinking has felt slow, but can you tell me more about whether you've experienced any physical slowing down of your movements, such as taking longer to get dressed or move around, since you've been feeling this way?\n\nPatient: I haven't really noticed myself physically moving slower or taking longer to do tasks like getting dressed. It’s more that absolutely everything feels like it requires a massive amount of effort because I am so constantly exhausted.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned that nothing brings you joy anymore, but have you experienced any activities or situations that you used to dislike but now find neutral or less bothersome since you've been feeling this way?\n\nPatient: I haven't really noticed anything like that happening. Rather than disliked things becoming more neutral, everything in general just feels completely flat, gray, and devoid of any energy or interest.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you've been taking care of your daily needs, such as bathing, dressing, and grooming, since you've been feeling this way, and have you noticed any difficulty or slowness in performing these tasks?\n\nPatient: Honestly, even simple daily tasks like taking a shower or getting ready feel like a massive chore now. I feel constantly wiped out, and doing these basic things takes so much more effort and time than it used to. It just leaves me feeling completely drained.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned this is your first episode of feeling this way and it started after a significant life event, but can you tell me if you've had any periods of elevated mood or irritability in the past, even if not as severe as your current state?\n\nPatient: No, I’ve never experienced anything like that. My mood has always been relatively stable and steady, without any periods of abnormally high energy or unusual irritability, until this recent downward turn.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any episodes of feeling excessively restless or agitated, where you couldn't sit still, since you've been feeling this way?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't felt restless or agitated at all. If anything, it’s the exact opposite—I feel incredibly sluggish and heavy. I can easily sit staring at my workbench for hours without moving a muscle.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned feeling sluggish and heavy, but can you tell me if there have been any times when you felt like you were moving or talking more slowly than usual, to the point where others might have noticed?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure about that, and I haven't noticed myself moving or talking slower. Since I've been keeping to myself and canceling plans lately, there hasn't really been anyone around to comment on it anyway.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed or has anyone else pointed out that you seem to be moving or responding more slowly than usual, even if it's just in small ways like slower reactions or taking longer to answer questions?\n\nPatient: I haven't really noticed myself moving or speaking slower, and no one has mentioned anything like that to me. My mind itself definitely feels quite slow and foggy lately, though, like it's taking forever just to process basic thoughts.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any instances where your physical movements or speech seemed slower to you or were pointed out by someone else as being slower, which might help differentiate between the severity of your current state?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really noticed my physical movements or speech being slower, and no one has mentioned anything like that to me. It's really just my mind that feels incredibly bogged down and sluggish.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if there have been moments, even small ones, where you felt like your body was moving in slow motion or that it took noticeable effort to initiate physical movements, which might help us understand your condition better?\n\nPatient: I wouldn't say I've thought of it as \"slow motion\" specifically, but initiating even basic physical tasks like taking a shower or walking to the grocery store requires an immense amount of physical effort. Everything just feels incredibly heavy, exhausting, and hard to start, and it leaves me completely wiped out.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any specific examples or days where it took you an unusually long time to perform daily tasks, such as getting out of bed, eating, or engaging in any physical activity, compared to your normal pace before this episode started?\n\nPatient: Yes, absolutely. I can sit in my workshop for an hour just staring at a project without ever starting it, and my brain feels so much like molasses that writing a simple email takes ages of rereading and second-guessing. I also regularly forget to eat until late afternoon, and basic tasks like walking to the grocery store now feel far more exhausting than a long bike ride ever did.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any specific days or moments where others, like friends or family, noticed that you were moving or responding more slowly than usual, which might have been different from your normal behavior?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't noticed anyone commenting on me moving or speaking slowly, and since I've been keeping to myself so much lately, I haven't really been around people enough for them to notice anyway.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned feeling exhausted and like everything requires a lot of effort, but can you specifically describe if you've experienced any days where it was unusually hard to get out of bed or start your daily activities, and if so, how that compared to your usual self before this episode?\n\nPatient: Yes, getting out of bed and starting the day has become a real uphill battle. Because I lie awake worrying until 2 or 3 in the morning, I wake up completely unrefreshed, and basic things like showering now feel like climbing a mountain. Before this, I was highly active, regularly going on long bike rides along Lake Michigan or spending hours working on my woodworking and model trains without a second thought.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe in more detail how your physical movements or ability to initiate actions have changed since you started feeling this way, such as any difficulty starting tasks or a feeling of being physically slowed down?\n\nPatient: I feel incredibly slowed down and really struggle to initiate any action. I often go down to my workshop and just sit there for long stretches staring at my projects, completely unable to actually start anything. Even simple physical tasks like taking a shower or walking to the grocery store now require a massive amount of physical effort, leaving me constantly wiped out.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned that this episode started after losing the consulting contract, but can you tell me if you think this event alone triggered your current state, or if you believe there were other underlying factors that contributed to how you're feeling now?\n\nPatient: While that last contract falling through was the tipping point, it was really the culmination of a very stressful year. Before that, two other major contracts had ended abruptly, leaving me out of the workforce for the first time since my twenties. The growing anxiety over my tightening savings and the sudden loss of my daily structure had been building up for months.\n\nDoctor: Given that this is your first episode of feeling this way and it started after a significant life event, can you tell me if you think the loss of the consulting contract was the sole trigger for your current state, or do you believe there might be other underlying factors that could suggest this is a more recurrent condition?\n\nPatient: This is definitely the first time I've ever felt like this, as I've worked steadily since my twenties without any mental health issues. While that final contract falling through was the breaking point, it followed a whole year of instability with other contracts ending abruptly and growing worries about my savings. It really feels tied to this sudden accumulation of career and financial stress, rather than being a recurring pattern from my past.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any moments where you felt like you were physically unable to move or respond, even when you wanted to, which might help us understand if your current state is more related to a severe depressive episode with psychomotor retardation or a less severe form?"

The fact that this is the patient's first episode and it started after a significant life event (the loss of the consulting contract) suggests that it could be a reactive depression. It's really just my mind that feels incredibly bogged down and sluggish.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if there have been moments, even small ones, where you felt like your body was moving in slow motion or that it took noticeable effort to initiate physical movements, which might help us understand your condition better?\n\nPatient: I wouldn't say I've thought of it as \"slow motion\" specifically, but initiating even basic physical tasks like taking a shower or walking to the grocery store requires an immense amount of physical effort.
